newsitem.title: ECUADOR: New Ecuador gov't to make fiscal accounts priority.
newsitem.headline: New Ecuador gov't to make fiscal accounts priority.

text.p: The public administration secretary of Ecuador's new government said Wednesday the government's main economic priority will be to put the country's deteriorating fiscal accounts into order.

Arturo Gangotena, whose role is similar to that of presidential chief of staff, added on local television that controlling inflation "will be one of the top priorities," of the new government headed by President Fabian Alarcon.
Alarcon was sworn in by Congress on Tuesday night after populist leader Abdala Bucaram, who had been in power six months, was ousted by Congress last week.
"Ecuadoreans have woken up from six months of bad dreams," said Gangotena, referring to the accusations of corruption and squandering levelled at Bucaram.
He said Alarcon's government would immediately start to evaluate the state of the fiscal accounts.
"After this six-month party we have to start looking into the state of the accounts," he said.
He added that the interim government, which will rule until August 1998, will respect all of Ecuador's foreign obligations.
